paired_analysis.method: Monte Carlo paired sign-flip randomization test of mean within-block time differences
paired_analysis.null_hypothesis: Under the randomized scenario order, the paired scenario labels have no effect on verification time.
paired_analysis.alternative_hypothesis: The paired scenario labels affect mean verification time.
paired_analysis.multiple_testing: Holm correction across all algorithm-size-scenario comparisons.

paired_analysis.diagnostics: Paired-difference Shapiro-Wilk, skewness, lag-1 correlation, and block trend are reported. The randomization test does not assume normally distributed differences; it relies on within-block randomized scenario order and no consequential carry-over between conditions.

practical_interpretation: Absolute time differences and percentage differences relative to matched baseline times are reported. No application-specific minimum practically meaningful time difference was supplied; statistical significance alone must not be treated as practical importance.
limitations: Each block uses one input and its one-byte modification; blocks are sequential measurements in one process, so temporal dependence and carry-over cannot be ruled out.

The attacker-recomputed digest scenario demonstrates that an unkeyed digest supplied by an attacker does not authenticate modified data; its passing verification is not successful tampering detection.
The timed operation includes the hash call and hmac.compare_digest only; input preparation, reference-digest generation, formatting, and file I/O are excluded.
The paired sign-flip test relies on the randomized within-block condition order and a sharp no-effect randomization null; inter-block environmental drift may still limit inference.
The data measure local Python hashlib and digest-comparison execution time, not network or storage costs.
outlier_policy: All validated raw observations are retained; none are automatically removed.
